ledger.summary: The Lady and the Teacher, marked by bead necklaces, sought and found the Well after much toil and drank; the Lady became as now and the Teacher about forty. About five years ago the Teacher left for the most ancient parts of the world. A month later three Dry Tree men came: old Geoffrey (the young knight who loved her long ago) and his two sons, last of twenty-one sworn seekers, saying it was fifty years since she vanished. She proved who she was. Geoffrey told her the Dry Tree had built a castle on the Scaur above Hampton, the Burg had grown great, and the Land of the Tower was ruined with grass in its Great City streets. They brought her to the Land of Abundance, where she lived; she bought the book from a monk. Dry Tree men often visited and asked her love.
ledger.geography_notes: The Dry Tree castle stands on the height of the Scaur above the little town of Hampton, hence "Hampton under Scaur". The Burg is the greatest power in the lands about. The Land of Abundance is a clearing in the wood whose folk are under the Fathers of the Thorn. Up-castle is named. The Teacher went to "the most ancient parts of the world".
